add_chart.description: Add a chart (bar, line or pie) of data already in a sheet of an existing spreadsheet; write the data first. categories is the range of labels (such as A2:A7) and each series' values is a range of numbers (such as B2:B7), all on sheet: one column or one row each, the same length, 1 to 50 cells. Up to 6 series; a pie takes exactly one. Formula cells work as data. anchor is the cell for the chart's top-left corner in Excel (default: beside the data). Omit id and it is returned; an id that exists replaces that chart. Charts follow inserted and deleted rows. The chart shows in the panel and is a native Excel chart in the .xlsx.

categories.description: Range of the labels on sheet, such as A2:A7.

series.description: One to six series; a pie takes exactly one.

values.description: Range of the numbers on sheet, such as B2:B7.

anchor.description: Cell for the chart's top-left corner in Excel, such as E2.

add_sheet.description: Add a sheet to an existing spreadsheet. name is unique, at most 31 characters, without [ ] : * ? / \. columns and rows work as in create_spreadsheet. position is the 0-based index to insert at (default: last).

columns.description: Optional settings per column, from column A: width in characters and a default format for the column's cells.

rows.description: Rows from the top; each row is an array of cells from column A.

items.description: A cell: a number, text, true/false, null for empty, or an object. Use the object for a formula ({"formula": "=SUM(B2:B9)"}) or to add format/style to a value ({"value": 700, "format": "currency", "style": "input"}). Text is always stored as text, even if it starts with =.

format.description: currency, currency0 (no decimals), percent, percent1, integer, decimal, date (value as YYYY-MM-DD), text, or an Excel number format such as 0.00" kg". currency is in the spreadsheet's currency (see create_spreadsheet's currency), else the money format the sheet already uses, else US dollars. Put text such as R$ or kr in quotes: "R$" #,##0.00.

append_rows.description: Add rows to the end of a sheet in an existing spreadsheet. Use it to write a large table in several calls: create_spreadsheet with the first rows and more_to_write true, then append_rows until the last call, which leaves more_to_write out. Cells work as in create_spreadsheet; formulas can refer to rows written earlier.

create_spreadsheet.description: Create a spreadsheet (an Excel workbook the user can preview and save as .xlsx). Use it when the user asks for a spreadsheet, workbook, Excel file or a table they will calculate with, such as a budget, cost model, forecast or schedule. Use real formulas for anything calculated, not numbers you worked out. Put inputs and assumptions in their own cells (style input), often on an Assumptions sheet, and refer to them from formulas. Give the header row style header and total rows style total. Every call returns errors for any formula that did not compute (such as #NAME? or #REF!): fix them with update_cells. For a large table, set more_to_write and continue with append_rows. Omit artifact_id; the app assigns it and returns it. To chart the data, call add_chart once it is written.

currency.description: The ISO code of the money in this spreadsheet, such as EUR, JPY or BRL, when it isn't US dollars: cells formatted currency show it.

delete_chart.description: Delete a chart from an existing spreadsheet by chart_id (add_chart and read_spreadsheet return it).

edit_sheet.description: Change a sheet's structure in an existing spreadsheet: rename_to renames it (formulas that refer to it are updated), delete removes it, columns replaces column settings, freeze_header sets row 1 frozen, delete_rows removes count rows starting at row from (1-based), insert_rows inserts rows before row at (1-based); a new row takes the formats and formulas of the row above where its cells are empty, and a total just below takes it in (SUM(B2:B7) becomes SUM(B2:B8)). With rows empty, it inserts count empty rows to fill with update_cells. Formulas that refer to moved rows are updated. title renames the spreadsheet itself (the name shown for the file, not a sheet); give it with any sheet, alone or with other changes.

count.description: With rows empty: how many empty rows to insert (default 1).

read_spreadsheet.description: Read an existing spreadsheet: for each cell its formula (if any) and computed value. Without sheet it lists the sheets with their sizes and returns the first sheet; range (such as A1:F40) limits what is returned. Large sheets are cut off with a note; read further with range. It also lists the charts (id, sheet, type, title, ranges).

update_cells.description: Change cells in an existing spreadsheet. For a block, give start (such as B2) and rows, a 2-D block of cells as in create_spreadsheet, going right and down from start. For cells scattered around the sheet, give cells instead, all in one call: [{"cell": "D4", "value": 25}, {"cell": "F9", "formula": "=SUM(F2:F8)"}]. null, or a cells item with only its address, clears a cell. Use it to change values, fix formulas that returned errors, or add a column. Other cells are left as they are.
